message: In the under-deck vertical Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) retrofit (C1), the tuning and added damping for the 1.9 Hertz mode has needed final confirmation, Structural Dynamics Lead. To check it I used vetted Den Hartog optimisation (the optimal TMD sizing (E4)) with detuned simulation (the detuned damping estimate (E8)). I found 400 kilograms at 1.86 Hertz with 0.086 TMD damping ratio holding 0.064 effective damping at plus 5 percent detune, according to Den Hartog, 1934. I propose retaining two 200 kilogram modules with slotted spring seats for re-tuning. My position: ready because tuning and damping survive detune. In the under-deck vertical Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) retrofit (C1), the crowd comfort and stroke margin has needed proof without changing deck appearance, Manager. To check it I used resonant baseline comparison (the resonant response calculation (E1)) with controlled response simulation (the controlled-response stroke estimate (E6)). I found about 0.20 metres per second squared versus 1.75 metres per second squared baseline with about 8.2 millimetres stroke within 30 millimetres clearance, according to Human Induced Vibrations of Steel Structures, 2008. I propose holding concealed midspan placement accessed from below. My position: ready because comfort and buildability are closed.
